name: Lewisville
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Lewisville, TX 2026
seo_description: Lewisville Lights tree lighting Dec 4, Breakfast with Santa and the Holiday Stroll Parade Dec 5, and Christmas at the Cabin at LLELA on Dec 12.
lede: The story of Christmas in Lewisville runs from a log house built after 1869 to the Old Town Holiday Stroll, where the city lights its Lewisville Lights tree every December. Lewisville itself dates to 1853, when Basdeal W. Lewis bought the land and the town's post office opened.
sections: The Old Town Holiday Stroll and its boat parade

The City of Lewisville calls the Old Town Holiday Stroll an annual event held the first Saturday of December, and it centers on Wayne Ferguson Plaza at 150 W. Church Street. Friday night brings a Kids Market, hayrides through Old Town, caroling and the Lewisville Lights tree lighting, presented by DCTA. Saturday adds a pancake breakfast with Santa and the Holiday Stroll Parade, which the city also calls the Huffines Auto Dealerships Lewisville Christmas Parade. The 2026 theme is Sailing into the Season, inspired by life on the water, with boats encouraged and Santa and Mrs. Claus riding as guests of honor on city floats and boats.
A log house found inside a house

The Minor-Porter Log House at LLELA has a story kids can repeat. William Tipton Minor came to Texas from Alabama in 1869 and built a log home for his new family on land in what is now Highland Village. Later the family added rooms and covered the logs with siding, so most people forgot a log house hid inside the Prairie House. When the property was sold and the house was to be torn down, the log home was found and donated to the city. It moved to LLELA in 2005 and was restored in 2005 and 2006. Each December LLELA decorates it for Christmas at the Cabin.
Riding the A-train to Old Town

Lewisville has three stops on the DCTA A-train: Hebron Station at 952 Lakeside Circle, Old Town Station at 617 E. Main Street and Highland Village/Lewisville Lake Station at 2998 N. Stemmons Freeway. The commuter line began running on June 20, 2011, from Denton to Trinity Mills Station in Carrollton, where riders change to DART's Green Line. DCTA presents the Lewisville Lights tree lighting, and at Christmas it runs Santa at the Station from the Downtown Denton Transit Center, on Saturday, December 5, 2026. For a longer train day, the Museum of the American Railroad in Frisco and the Interurban Railway Museum in Plano are a drive away.

kidfact: At LLELA a real log house spent decades hiding inside a bigger house covered in siding, and it was found only when the bigger house was about to be torn down.
faq: Basdeal W. Lewis bought the Hallford properties and established Lewisville in 1853, the year its post office opened, according to the Handbook of Texas. A gristmill followed in 1862, the county's first cotton gin came by 1867 and the Dallas and Wichita Railway arrived in 1881. The town incorporated in 1925.
Where is the Lewisville tree lighting?

The Lewisville Lights tree lighting is part of the Old Town Holiday Stroll at Wayne Ferguson Plaza, 150 W. Church Street. In 2026 it is on Friday, December 4, at 6:45 pm, presented by DCTA. Caroling starts at 6:30 pm, and the Santa Clause 2 plays in the plaza at 7 pm.
What is the Minor-Porter Log House at LLELA?

It is a log home built after William Tipton Minor came to Texas in 1869. It was hidden inside a larger house, found before demolition, donated to the City of Lewisville, moved to LLELA in 2005 and restored in 2005 and 2006. LLELA opens it on the third Saturday of most months and at Christmas at the Cabin.
Can we take the train to Lewisville's Christmas events?

The DCTA A-train stops at Old Town Station, 617 E. Main Street, as well as Hebron and Highland Village/Lewisville Lake stations. The Holiday Stroll is in Old Town, and DCTA presents the tree lighting. Riders from Dallas can change to the A-train at Trinity Mills Station, which DART also serves.
Why are there boats in the Lewisville Christmas parade?

The 2026 Holiday Stroll Parade theme is Sailing into the Season. The city asks entries to combine holiday spirit with the fun, beauty and character of life on the water, and it encourages boats and watercraft. Prizes include a $1,500 Captain's Award, a Best Nautical Theme award and an Ahoy award for Santa.
How did Lewisville grow into a big city?

The Handbook of Texas says the expanded Lake Lewisville dam, Interstate 35E and DFW Airport pushed growth, and later defense, aerospace and computer industries and Vista Ridge Mall added more. The Texas Almanac lists 3,956 people in 1960 and 111,822 at the 2020 census.
